Multisite Analysis of Pharmacists Actions that lead to Cost Avoidance

Authors

Josh DeClercq

Department of Biostatistics

Vanderbilt University Medical Center

Published

June 9, 2026

1 Study Overview

1.1 Background

The purpose of this study is to evaluate direct cost avoidance from pharmacist interventions that identify inappropriate (ineffective or unsafe) medication use and result in medication discontinuation, dose adjustment, or medication switch (collectively termed medication outcome henceforth).

1.2 Methods

  • Prospective multisite cohort study (n = 16)

  • Inclusion criteria:

    • Adult and pediatric patients prescribed specialty medications from a health-system (regardless of their filling pharmacy)
    • At least one fill of a specialty medication
    • At least one intervention that led to a medication outcome of interest in the study period (6 months)

  • Exclusion criteria:

    • Patients with a medication outcome completed due to non-clinical reason

1.3 Outcomes

The study had three aims. The first aim was to quantify pharmacist interventions that resulted in a discontinuation, switch, or dose/formulation change of a specialty medication. Outcomes for this aim included counts of interventions performed by each medication outcome and intervention reasons.

Secondly, we aimed to estimate the pTC associated with each intervention. The final pTC score for each intervention was analyzed according to medication outcome, intervention reason, and clinical area.

Finally, we approximated direct cost avoidance resulting from pharmacist interventions. Outcomes included the total direct cost avoidance over six months of interventions, median cost avoided per intervention, and median cost avoided by medication outcome, intervention reason, and clinical area.
